title: Kirkwood council stalls noise ordinance, cites lack of enforcement expertise
text:

Kirkwood council stalls noise ordinance, cites lack of enforcement expertise
City attorney Darren said he would email a list of recommended changes after council members questioned whether decibel measurements would hold up without proper equipment.
The Kirkwood City Council postponed action on a proposed noise ordinance during a work session Thursday, Oct. 1, after members said they lacked the expertise to decide how the rules would be enforced.
ENFORCEMENT QUESTIONS Council member Burquette said enforcement should be the starting point for any new rule. "I would just ask that then we focus on what's enforceable and that we're putting things in that are enforceable," Burquette said, adding that no one was present to speak to enforcement.
A council member raised concerns that measuring decibels at the property line of the emitting source versus the receiving property would produce different results depending on distance between properties.
EQUIPMENT CONCERNS A council member identified as Deb said the city likely does not own a calibrated decibel meter. "I don't know if the city currently has a calibrated decibel meter or not, but certainly it," she said, noting the draft ordinance requires readings from "a properly calibrated decelerator." She questioned whether a phone-based meter would be legally sufficient, saying, "I don't know that phones are necessarily that."
Deb also said the city lacks an outside expert. "I don't think we have an acoustical engineer on staff," she said, adding that other ordinances use broader terms like "a sound level meter" without clarity on consequences or who would enforce them, whether code enforcement or police.
WHAT HAPPENS NEXT Darren, identified as the city's attorney, said he would email his list of recommended changes. Council members discussed forming a subcommittee or work session involving an outside expert before making further decisions.
Meanwhile, council members said existing tools, including special use permits, would continue to address current noise complaints near Billy G's while the broader ordinance is reworked. "We move that one forward tonight. We follow the SUP," a council member said.
